title: Somatic Mutations Drive Distinct Imaging Phenotypes in Lung Cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Somatic Mutations Drive Distinct Imaging Phenotypes in Lung Cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Tumors are characterized by somatic mutations that drive biological processes ultimately reflected in tumor phenotype.

evidence.text: Tumors are characterized by somatic mutations that drive biological processes ultimately reflected in tumor phenotype.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Somatic Mutations Drive Distinct Imaging Phenotypes in Lung Cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】Here we demonstrate how imaging phenotypes can be connected to somatic mutations through an integrated analysis of independent datasets of 763 lung adenocarcinoma patients with somatic mutation testing and engineered CT image analytics.

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】We developed radiomic signatures capable of distinguishing between tumor genotypes in a discovery cohort (n = 353) and verified them in an independent validation cohort (n = 352).

evidence.text: Here we demonstrate how imaging phenotypes can be connected to somatic mutations through an integrated analysis of independent datasets of 763 lung adenocarcinoma patients with somatic mutation testing and engineered CT image analytics.
We developed radiomic signatures capable of distinguishing between tumor genotypes in a discovery cohort (n = 353) and verified them in an independent validation cohort (n = 352).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Somatic Mutations Drive Distinct Imaging Phenotypes in Lung Cancer》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】We found a radiomic signature related to radiographic heterogeneity that successfully discriminated between EGFR+ and EGFR- cases (AUC = 0.69).

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】Combining this signature with a clinical model of EGFR status (AUC = 0.70) significantly improved prediction accuracy (AUC = 0.75).

evidence.text: We found a radiomic signature related to radiographic heterogeneity that successfully discriminated between EGFR+ and EGFR- cases (AUC = 0.69).
Combining this signature with a clinical model of EGFR status (AUC = 0.70) significantly improved prediction accuracy (AUC = 0.75).
